sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A large palm endemic to Mauritius, with a bottle-shaped swelling near the base of the trunk that narrows toward the crown. It can reach about 18 m. Kew lists the species as extinct in Mauritius, but sources reported one individual at Curepipe Botanic Garden in 2024; its current condition is not confirmed here.

sections.title: Leaves and fruit
sections.text: Long pinnate leaves form a crown at the top of the trunk; ripe fruits are red. The plate shows the general habit but does not clearly depict the characteristic basal swelling.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: No food use is documented in the sources consulted.
